title: The Great Molasses Flood — जब बोस्टन की सड़कों पर शीरे की लहर दौड़ी

lines.text: The afternoon of 15 January 1919. Boston's North End, Commercial Street.
lines.visual: slow push across the BPL panorama of the site; date types on

lines.text: From a giant tank, 2,300,000 gallons of molasses poured into the streets.
lines.visual: the panorama darkens; a brown wash spreads along the street line

lines.text: The next day's Boston Post reported the wave as 50 feet high; that figure is disputed.
lines.visual: cut to the Post masthead and deck; highlight '50 Feet High'; a stamp 'विवादित'

lines.text: By midnight, the paper counted 11 dead and more than 50 injured.
lines.visual: the Post headline '11 DEAD, 50 HURT' underlined

lines.text: Sweet, thick molasses. How could it kill anyone?
lines.visual: title card on the evidence wall

lines.text: The answer lies in a newspaper of that time, and in the city's account written a century later.
lines.visual: two labelled cards pin to the wall: the Post (1919) and the City of Boston (retrospective)

lines.text: The story begins with a giant tank standing on Commercial Street.
lines.visual: the tank photo, slow push-in

lines.text: According to the City of Boston's account, the tank was built in 1915 by the Purity Distilling Company.
lines.visual: City of Boston source card; year types on

lines.text: According to the city, it was 50 feet tall and held about 2.3 million gallons of molasses.
lines.visual: a scale bar rises beside the tank to 50 ft

lines.text: The Boston Post printed the same quantity in its report: 2,300,000 gallons.
lines.visual: the Post deck, '2,300,000 Gallons' highlighted

lines.text: So on this figure, the newspaper of the time and the city's later account agree.
lines.visual: the two source cards drawn together by a thread

lines.text: The city's account records one more thing.
lines.visual: City of Boston card brought forward

lines.text: The tank, it is reported, had been leaking before the disaster.
lines.visual: the tank photo; slow drips drawn down its side, labelled 'बताया गया'

lines.text: It was something like a warning sign.
lines.visual: hold on the tank; the light dims

lines.text: 15 January 1919, after midday. The tank gave way.
lines.visual: the tank photo cracks to black

lines.text: According to the City of Boston, several causes came together.
lines.visual: City of Boston card; three empty slots appear

lines.text: Weak construction, changes in temperature, and a large shipment of molasses.
lines.visual: the three slots fill one by one

lines.text: According to the Boston Post, the molasses spread over Commercial Street and its waterfront.
lines.visual: the area map; the flooded zone fills along Commercial Street

lines.text: From Charter Street to the southern end of North End Park.
lines.visual: a route line runs from Charter Street to North End Park

lines.text: According to the city's account, the wave moved at about 35 miles an hour.
lines.visual: a speed figure counts up on the map; labelled as an estimate

lines.text: How high the wave was is disputed: the sources do not agree.
lines.visual: the Post's '50 Feet High' beside a question mark

lines.text: The Post wrote 50 feet, about as tall as the tank is in the city's account.
lines.visual: the 50 ft scale bar from the tank slides beside the headline

lines.text: According to many later accounts, it was much lower.
lines.visual: the bar lowers and blurs; label 'बाद के अनुमान'

lines.text: In the Post's words, the sticky flood caught more than 100 men, women and children.
lines.visual: the Post column, the passage highlighted

lines.text: Buildings, horse teams, motor cars and streetcars. Whatever stood in its path was crushed.
lines.visual: pan across the wreckage photo

lines.text: The elevated railway structure overhead did not survive either.
lines.visual: the elevated-railway photo; slow tilt up the bent structure

lines.text: The paper wrote that the black, reeking mass struck the buildings facing Copp's Hill.
lines.visual: the map; an arrow drives towards Copp's Hill

lines.text: And then swept back towards the harbour.
lines.visual: the arrow swings back to the harbour

lines.text: Among the dead was an engineer of Engine 31 of the Boston Fire Department.
lines.visual: the Post's list of the known dead; one name highlighted

lines.text: The Post printed his name as George Lahey.
lines.visual: the name 'GEORGE LAHEY' lit in the list

lines.text: Among the dead was also a girl of about 14, still unidentified when the paper went to press.
lines.visual: the Post's 'unidentified dead' paragraph

lines.text: She wore a grey jacket, and her bag carried an employment tag of the Revere Rubber Company.
lines.visual: the words 'Revere Rubber Company' highlighted; hold

lines.text: Ambulances were rushed to the scene from every part of the city.
lines.visual: the Post's bird's-eye photo; its caption highlighted

lines.text: Rescue work went on at the North End Park playground.
lines.visual: push into the playground area of the photo

lines.text: Dead horses, cats and dogs were carted away, load after load.
lines.visual: the panorama, slow drift across the wreckage

lines.text: Boston's only trolley freight terminal lay in ruins.
lines.visual: hold on the ruined buildings

lines.text: The Post's first count was 11 dead: a woman, a girl and nine men.
lines.visual: a tally types on: 11

lines.text: But the number did not stop there.
lines.visual: the tally holds, then a second card slides in

lines.text: According to the City of Boston, 21 people died in the end, and about 150 were injured.
lines.visual: the tally rolls from 11 to 21; City of Boston card

lines.text: Now the biggest question: how did it happen?
lines.visual: the evidence wall; a red thread from the tank to two cards

lines.text: The next day, the Boston Post reported that the state police chemist, W. L. Wedger, had reached a positive conclusion.
lines.visual: the Post's 'INTERNAL EXPLOSION WAS CAUSE, SAYS STATE CHEMIST' column

lines.text: According to him, the tank had not collapsed; there had been an explosion inside it.
lines.visual: the words 'internal explosion' highlighted

lines.text: That was the early, disputed theory of the time. Later findings pointed another way.
lines.visual: a stamp 'शुरुआती सिद्धांत' over the column

lines.text: According to the city's account, structural engineers later found that the tank's walls were too thin.
lines.visual: City of Boston card; a cross-section of a wall drawn thin

lines.text: And that its material was prone to cracking.
lines.visual: a crack runs through the diagram

lines.text: According to the city's account, in 1925 a court-appointed auditor held the owners' negligence responsible.
lines.visual: a dated card '1925' pins over the thread's end

lines.text: So, unlike the explosion claimed on the first day, the later findings point to the tank's construction and to negligence.
lines.visual: the explosion card fades; the negligence card stays lit

lines.text: The front page of the same newspaper carried another story.
lines.visual: pull back to the whole Post front page

lines.text: The Prohibition amendment had been ratified by 35 states, and just one more was needed.
lines.visual: '35 STATES ON DRY LAW LIST' highlighted

lines.text: The molasses wave and Prohibition: both stories ran side by side on one page.
lines.visual: the two columns lit side by side

lines.text: This film claims no link between them; just the same day, the same page.
lines.visual: hold on the full page; slow fade of the highlights

lines.text: On the first day, the Post wrote that the molasses had been released in some manner yet unexplained.
lines.visual: the Post column 'released in some manner yet unexplained' highlighted

lines.text: Later, the causes were recorded: walls too thin and, according to the auditor, the owners' negligence.
lines.visual: the thin-wall diagram and the 1925 card return beside the tank photo

lines.text: The cost of that afternoon: 21 lives.
lines.visual: the panorama; the tally 21 holds in silence

lines.text: This wave of molasses is a reminder of how much it matters to inspect the structures a city trusts.
lines.visual: slow pull-back to the whole evidence wall; fade to black
